input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
input.rationale: Section 22 is the only audit/verification right binding us, and it meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency limited to once in any twelve-month period; at least thirty days' prior written notice; normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption; off-site where practicable via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (§ 22.1); Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent, in which case we pay reasonable costs plus the undisputed shortfall (§ 22.2). The walk-away risk is expressly excluded — Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, nor unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information. Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are our Confidential Information, use limited to enforcement, copy of the final report, and payment of a shortfall resolves the issue). No other inspection, verification, monitoring or remote-access right binding us appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.
